name: Awadhi

ancestors.notes: Indo-Aryan — the classification node this language sits under.

Eastern Hindi sibling: Awadhi and Bhojpuri share the same Devanagari letter-to-breathy-voice mapping and the retention of the inherent vowel /a/ rather than Standard Hindi's /ə/ (Saksena 1971; Masica 1991).

notes: Awadhi (अवधी), an Eastern Hindi / Indo-Aryan language of the Awadh region of Uttar Pradesh, India (the language of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas). SKELETON: grapheme inventory now specified (letter-to-phoneme table for the Devanagari abugida), modelled on the sibling Eastern Hindi language Bhojpuri (`bho`), which the literature groups with Awadhi under the same Eastern Hindi umbrella sharing an /a/ (not schwa) inherent vowel and a four-way laryngeal (voice/breathy-voice) stop series (Saksena 1971, 'Evolution of Awadhi'; Masica 1991). Unlike Standard Hindi, no schwa-deletion rule is asserted: the inherent vowel of a Devanagari consonant letter in Awadhi is /a/, not /ə/, so there is no schwa to delete (contrast `hi`, whose HI_SCHWA_FINAL_* rules exist precisely because Standard Hindi's inherent vowel IS /ə/). Nukta letters ड़/ढ़ (flap series) are included; the learned nukta letters क़/ख़/ग़/ज़/फ़ (Perso-Arabic loans) are not attested as phonemically distinct in rural Awadhi speech per Saksena and are therefore left unmapped rather than asserted. श/ष/स are merged to /s/: unlike Standard Hindi's spelling-pronunciation, the sibilant contrast of Sanskrit tatsama spelling is not maintained in Awadhi speech (Masica 1991: 97, sibilant merger is general in Eastern Hindi). STRESS EXEMPTION: word stress in Awadhi, as in the wider Hindi belt, is not lexically contrastive and is predictable from syllable weight rather than from spelling; no `stress` block is declared (cf. `hi`, which documents the same exemption). PHONEME INVENTORY: PHOIBLE (glottocode awad1243) records the same four-way stop series and retroflex flap using combining-tilde-under breathy notation (b̤, d̪̤, ɖ̤, ɟ̤ʝ, ɡʱ, l̤, m̤, r̤, ɽ̤) and a palatal affricate as cç/cçʰ; this spec uses the postaspirate ʱ convention (bʱ, d̪ʱ, ɖʱ, dʒʱ, ɡʱ) and tʃ/dʒ already standard across this dataset's Indic specs (`hi`, `bho`) — the same phonemes, a different diacritic convention. Awadhi is also historically written in the Kaithi and Perso-Arabic scripts; input is assumed to be Devanagari. This spec reads ⟨ऩ⟩, ⟨ऱ⟩ and ⟨ऴ⟩ as their base letters ⟨न⟩ [n], ⟨र⟩ [r] and ⟨ल⟩ [l], because the inventory has no separate phoneme for them. This spec has no ⟨ळ⟩, so ⟨ऴ⟩ takes the value of ⟨ल⟩.

sources.notes: U+0929 DEVANAGARI LETTER NNNA: "for transcribing Dravidian alveolar n"; U+0931 DEVANAGARI LETTER RRA: "for transcribing Dravidian alveolar r", "half form is represented as \"Eyelash RA\""; U+0934 DEVANAGARI LETTER LLLA: "for transcribing Dravidian l".
